barriers.reason: A Thursday 11:30 AM session plus a 4-hour prescription ends around 3:30 PM, when the grandkids get out of school at 3; the neighbor works Thursdays and the daughter works until 6:30, so no one is available to care for the children during/after treatment.

alternatives.text: Ask the dialysis unit for a later Thursday chair time or move Thursday to a day when childcare is available (for example Saturday, when the daughter is home).
Message the unit social worker to help arrange Thursday coverage and explore benefits or resources that support the patient's caregiving situation.
Refer to the home dialysis program to discuss peritoneal or home hemodialysis as a conversation, not a guaranteed fix, given its own space, supply, training, and support requirements.

barriers.reason: The patient eats what the children eat (hot dogs, macaroni and cheese) and has limited access to fresh renal-friendly produce, making a low-phosphorus/low-potassium diet with fresh produce hard to follow.

alternatives.text: Have the unit dietitian rebuild the diet around foods the patient can actually get, building on the chairside Tuesday visit the patient already accepts.
Apply for SNAP through Illinois ABE (abe.illinois.gov) to improve income-based food purchasing power; very low-income households may qualify for expedited benefits within 7 days.

Use the Greater Chicago Food Depository locator to find pantries open on the patient's non-treatment days, and pair pantry use with renal-dietitian guidance because pantry food is often not renal-friendly.
